datasets.title: Satellite detected waters extents, as of 28 August 2019 over Khartoum State, Sudan
datasets.description: UNOSAT code: FL20190815SDN This map illustrates satellite-detected surface water in Khartoum State, Sudan as observed from SPOT-6 imagery acquired on 28 August 2019. Within the analysed extent of about 3,200 km2, a total about 97 km2 of lands appear to be flooded as of 28 August 2019. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to UNITAR - UNOSAT.. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/satellite-detected-waters-extents-as-of-28-august-2019-over-khartoum-state-sudan]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts interpreted SPOT-6 satellite imagery acquired on 28 August 2019 over Khartoum State, comparing multi-temporal images to identify notable changes in surface water extent. The analysis delineated flooded areas totaling approximately 97 km² within a 3,200 km² study area, producing vector geometries with area measurements in hectares and square meters.

sources.name: UN Operational Satellite Applications Programme (UNOSAT)
sources.description: Satellite imagery analysis using SPOT-6 data to detect and map surface water extents through visual interpretation and multi-temporal image comparison
